the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

[('memory', 'ARC: classify compartments by count of marked cells', 'For ARC task-1758d474, grids are divided by full-color separator rows/columns into rectangular compartments. Count the sparse cells that differ from the compartment background. Output one cell per compartment: use color 1 when the compartment contains at least two marked cells; otherwise use the background color. Keep output compartment layout in original row/column order. Verified on multiple demos and test: test separators 9, background 3, marks 8; at least two 8s => 1, otherwise 3. Additional solved instance: separators were color 2, compartment background 5, marked cells 9; separator bands split a 9x11 grid into 2x3 compartments. Counts by compartment were [[1,1,1],[2,2,2]], so output was [[5,5,5],[1,1,1]]. This also confirms singleton marked compartments stay background, while exactly two marks map to 1. This recurrence also appeared with separator 8, background 7, and marks 9: full separator rows/columns split an 11x14 grid into 3x5 compartments; output was [[7,1,1,7,1],[1,7,7,7,1],[1,1,7,1,1]]. Rule remains at least two marks -> 1, otherwise background; dynamically identify palette roles rather than assuming colors. Carefully count every cell in each compartment (the initial attempt missed a second mark in the last middle compartment).

Additional confirmed recurrence (24x9): separator color 0, separator rows at 4,9,14,19 and separator column 4 split the grid into 5x2 compartments. Background 7, marks 2; output 1 for at least two marks, otherwise 7. Counts gave output [[1,7],[1,1],[1,7],[1,7],[1,1]], confirmed correct on the first submission. Check band boundaries carefully: compartments cover rows 0-3, 5-8, 10-13, 15-18, 20-23 and columns 0-3 / 5-8.

Confirmed another task-1758d474 test (15x14): separator color 7 formed full rows 3, 7, 11 and columns 2, 5, 8, 11. This split the nonseparator cells into 4x5 compartments with background 6 and marks 8. Output 1 for at least two 8s, otherwise 6: [[6,1,1,1,1],[1,6,6,1,6],[6,1,6,1,6],[1,6,6,1,1]]. Correct on the first submission. When counting, exclude all separator bands and preserve the original compartment order.

Confirmed current task test (11x15): separator 9 at rows 2,5,8 and columns 3,7,11; background 5, sparse marks 2. The four-by-four count matrix (row/column compartment order) was [[1,1,2,1],[1,2,1,1],[1,1,2,2],[2,1,2,1]], so correct output was [[5,5,1,5],[5,1,5,5],[5,5,1,1],[1,5,1,5]]. Important: output 1 only for counts >=2; a single mark stays background. Explicitly count each compartment before mapping; the first two incorrect submissions resulted from misclassifying one-count cells as output 1.

Confirmed another task-1758d474 test (24x24): separator color 2 at full rows 4, 9, 14, 19 and full columns 4, 9, 14, 19 (zero-based). This yields a 5x5 arrangement of 4x4 compartments. Background 7, marked cells 4. Counts by compartment were [[1,2,1,1,2],[2,2,1,1,1],[2,1,1,1,2],[1,2,1,1,1],[2,1,1,2,1]], so output [[7,1,7,7,1],[1,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,7,1],[7,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,1,7]]. Correct on the first submission. This reinforces that output value 1 means at least two marks; one mark maps to background.')]

steps.input: rs=[(0,4),(5,9),(10,14),(15,19),(20,24)]; cs=[(0,4),(5,9),(10,14)]; counts=[[sum(g[r][c]==4 for r in range(a,b) for c in range(x,y)) for x,y in cs] for a,b in rs]; counts, [[1 if n>=2 else 8 for n in row] for row in counts]
